request.text:
The glade colony took root. Within a season it had its walls and its brood halls, and not one of its ants drank raw.

Then one night Oleander set a slender vial on the Queen's table: beetle glass, capped in brass, full of a light that did not stain it. "The beetles hold it," he said. "And it never touches them."

voice.description: A wise elderly woman narrator: deep, rich and velvety, calm and a little solemn, with long pauses and a hint of mystery in her voice. She speaks English with a soft, neutral accent, clearly and unhurried, close to the microphone in a quiet room, as if telling a tale to children by lantern light.
